items.title: Peter Vacher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001
items.q: Whether they have something that is so special that others this side of the pond might learn from it well I’ll leave others to say. But we have produced some fine players if you think of someone like Joe Temperley, presently with the Lincoln Center Jazz Orchestra.

ctx.x: I want to tell you about Keith Ingham, who you are aware of, of course. I asked him about American musicians going to England and embracing English music, like he came over here, and he said, “Well we don’t have anything as good as American jazz.” What’s your reaction to that statement?

I think there’s a whole built-in thing which seems to imply that because America is the home of the music that Americans must be its best practitioners. And I grew up with that. But I think a little bit of perspective starts to say that today jazz is an international music. It’s a music of all nations. And I think I’d be prepared to say that we have some very fine players. Whether they have something that is so special that others this side of the pond might learn from it well I’ll leave others to say. But we…
Yeah, and I’m not sure he was just talking about the musicians either. But he thought that jazz in itself was, I guess, better for him than any kind of music that he would have found in England.
